steps.prompt: A king hemmed in by its own pawns on the back rank can be mated by a rook or queen along that rank. This is the most common beginner checkmate.
steps.explanation: A king hemmed in by its own pawns on the back rank can be mated by a rook or queen along that rank. This is the most common beginner checkmate.

steps.prompt: Trade rooks with a checkmate: capture on d8.
steps.explanation: Rxd8 is check and the pawns on f7, g7 and h7 take away the king's escape squares.
steps.hint: Capture the rook with your rook.

steps.prompt: White threatens Rd8 mate. Black to move: give the king air (luft) with a pawn move.
steps.explanation: Moving one pawn makes an escape square, so a back-rank check is no longer mate.
steps.hint: Move a pawn in front of the king by one or two squares.
